world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Mahapatra, B. P. 2002 subclassification comment on Glottolog; no grammar or phonology of Reli located.

sources.citation: Same volume (Mahapatra et al. 2002), chapter 'Sambalpuri', printed p. 79 (PDF p. 100) - NOT Relli.
sources.note: About Sambalpuri, not Relli: 'Stress in Sambalpuri does not appear to be phonemic. Word when uttered in isolation is generally stressed and the initial syllable of each breath group bears stress'. This is the only occurrence of the word 'stress' in the whole 615-page volume's text layer; nothing comparable is said for Relli.

sources.citation: Mahapatra, B. P., C. Sivashanmugam & S. S. Bhattacharya (supervision); S. P. Datta (chief co-ordinator). 2002. Linguistic Survey of India: Special Studies: Orissa. Kolkata: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. Chapter 'Relli' by S. P. Datta, pp. 112-135 (= PDF pp. 133-156 of the archive.org scan).
sources.note: Silent on stress. The chapter's 'Supra-segmental' section (printed p. 113, PDF p. 134, checked on the page image) lists only '1. /~/ Nasalization is phonemic. 2. Length is predictable in the monosyllabic words ending in close syllable.' No stress/accent/juncture/intonation heading anywhere in the chapter (text layer of PDF pp. 133-157 scanned for stress|accent|junctur|intonat|tone|pitch; only 'syllable' in morphological contexts). Phonology sections present: phonemic inventory, phonemic description and distribution, allophonic distribution, diphthongs, consonant clusters, then comparative not…
